paragraphs.text: Behind the Ticker is brought to you by UX Wealth Partners. If you're a TAMP user and you're sick and tired of the legacy technology they are run on and you want more customization and flexibility, as well as an AI-driven model marketplace, UX Wealth Partners is your destination. On top of that, they have institutional trading. So if you are an ETF issuer or an SMA provider looking for outsourced institutional trading, UX Wealth can also be your destination. So check out uxwp.com to find out all the ways UX Wealth Partners can help grow and make your practice more efficient.

Welcome to Behind the Ticker. Today we have on Kirsten Chang. She is from Vetify and we are talking about the Exchange ETF Conference, which is right around the corner. It is the big one. 23rd, 24th, 25th, and the 26th of March. We will be in Vegas this year. Everybody in the ETF industry, the whole landscape, as well as hundreds and hundreds of financial advisors. There's plenty to do. We talk about the agenda. We also talk about some of the other fun events and things that will be going on while we're all together. So without further ado, please welcome Kirsten Chang.
Hi, Kirsten. Welcome to the show. Hey, Brad. Happy Friday. Thanks so much for having me on. Great to be with you.
So before we get started, why don't you tell everybody a bit about your background and how you ended up at your current role over at Vetify?

Yeah, sure thing. So I started out at CNBC. I got a job as a producer right out of college, and I spent more than a decade there, first on Squawk Box, which is the morning show. Then I moved on to work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange with Bob Bizani, one and only, covering the stock markets and helping start up his weekly show, ETF Edge. So Bob and I used to attend this exchange conference every year, which of course used to always be in Miami. And we would kind of get together with the close-knit ETF community, sit down with CEOs, thought leaders, cover the latest, greatest trends in the business. So I became pretty close with Tom Lydon, of course, who started up Vetify, Dave Noddick,

Todd Rosenbluth as well. So they kind of approached me once they caught wind of my leaving CNBC when I wanted to move back to the West Coast and asked if I was interested in developing more of my own voice. And because exchange always fell in the first quarter of the year, we really took those conversations as kind of setting the stage for the markets. So whatever resonated at the conference was really what drove investor and advisor interest for the rest of the year. So I was always very fascinated by that community.

I think I've started my day off for the last 20 years with Squawk Box. There you go. Joe, Becky, and Andrew. Joe, Becky, and Andrew. And I love when Joe and Andrew go after it, particularly during political. But it's, yeah, I'm so very familiar with the show. Yeah, colorful cast of characters. Yeah, it is. It's great. sit there with my coffee and turn on Squawk Box. It's like automatic for me. Well, thanks for watching. Yeah. So I have to ask, before we kind of get into the topic, which we're going to talk about the Exchange ETF Conference, it's coming up here in a couple of weeks. Any hobbies? What do you like to do when you're not working?

Oh, well, I love rock climbing. I like to do that when I can, although I am pregnant now, so I can't really be doing that these days. But I normally love rock climbing. I like to go skiing. I know you were just in Colorado. That's one of my favorite spots to go to hit the slopes there. I also really enjoy kind of hiking, which is a big reason I moved back west. I really wanted that exposure to nature and the outdoors. like karaoke and my free time. Yeah. And just kind of watching nerdy movies and things like that. How about yourself?

Oh, I, well, you're having a baby. I have two young ones. So my days are, basically making sure my little one doesn't have to go to the emergency room for busting his head on something, doing backflips off the couch and my daughter's in soccer and tennis and all the stuff. So it's great, though. It's great. Um, well, let's talk really briefly at first, because, um, at Vetify, you're not just putting on a conference, right? So what is Vetify kind of as a whole? What do they do? How do they help service clients? um, you guys have a big company. So if you could, um, just kind of give everybody a little bit about what they do outside of just putting on this wonderful conference once a year.
Yeah.

Great question. Vetify is a lot of things. It's, it's an index provider. We pair with index partners to launch actual ETF products. Um, we are a data company. We have all the latest data trends. We watch the flows carefully performance. We have a digital distribution company. So we do regular webcasts where we educate advisors, kind of bridge the gap between advisors and issuers, a lot of letting them know what's under the hood of these companies because they're in the funds because there's so many ETFs out there, 4,000. So we really have to kind of be careful and sifting through the noise and letting people know what's out there, what they can recommend to their clients, what makes sense in the current market environment.

So a lot of educational work there. Um, I write weekly articles based on the trends that I'm seeing. I moderate these webcasts on a regular basis. Um, so a lot of, a lot of just kind of being the one-stop shop for ETF data and information for advisors and, and investors, um, ultimately.

Yeah, no, I've been on the website a handful of times. There's a breadth of information and you're kind of, the behemoth in the room when it comes to all things ETFs. And so, um, yeah, I, I use it as a resource often, but we're here to talk about the big one, the exchange ETF conference. It is the ETF conference, uh, of the year now in Vegas used to be in Miami. So big change this year. So really how did the, conference come about and like, what is the, the point of getting all of us together for a handful of days now in Vegas?

Yeah. So it's, it's the world's largest ETF conference. Um, it has been going on for a number of years, I think more than a decade now. I just joined Vetify last year, but I know it's been going on for long before that because I used to attend those on the other side of things. So it's kind of wild and wonderful to be on the, on the action, part of the action and the inside of it all. But kind of the idea is to offer advisors, you mentioned Vegas, they say what happens in Vegas stays in Vegas. While that might be true, we're, we're hoping our advisors take away plenty of tangible advice home to their clients. We want them to, have actionable insights and analysis that includes updated

Tools kind of to enhance their business practice and better themselves and their businesses. And again, we want to set the stage for the, for the rest of the year in terms of the market conversations and what's really driving the trends. Um, so yeah, it's essentially a way to give advisors a playbook to prepare them for what's ahead, never a dull moment in the market these days. Yeah. Well, that's true.

Um, so this conference is pretty unique. I go to a lot of conferences. What do you think kind of sets this apart from other financial conferences? Cause there's like 30 of them every year. And this one seems it has always been, a must go to and very well attended. So what do you think is kind of the main reason for that?

Yeah. Um, I think again, we, we kind of, we're supposed to be the, the one-stop shop for everything ETF. So we're, we're bringing all the biggest issuers and asset management provide, they're there, they're part of our partnership. Um, they're going to give us the greatest insights into what's going on with the latest products. We also have keynote speakers that always draw a lot of attention. David Kelly, people love listening to for the latest macro market analysis. Ian Bremmer is going to be there to help cap things off and kind of make some sense of what in the world is going on with, with trade wars, tariffs and geopolitics right now, which is certainly top of mind. And I think just the idea that, as, as students of the trade advisors always

Have to keep learning. They have to, they can't get comfortable or complacent with what they know. They have to keep learning. So they have to keep listening and learning and educating themselves so they can go home and talk about the evolution of, of the markets and educate their clients on what else is out there and what's new. I think our conference is a great place to do that in person.

Yeah, I agree. there's a ton of ETF issuers. There's a ton of service providers. There's all the different facets that attend this conference, but really as an advisor, there is so much, there's so much more than just ETFs, ETFs, ETFs. And I think as a financial advisor, given the fact that they get a massive discount for coming, right? Like it's a perfect conference for, for financial advisors to attend. And, um, but I think what are the big trends? What are the big themes this year that attendees can expect at this year's conference, both kind of within ETFs and kind of the broader investment landscape?

Yeah. So, the ETF industry has evolved and so has the agenda. A lot of the topics we'll be covering will range from hot button issues like private credit ETFs and hedge fund led multi-asset ETFs. And we'll also be talking about actively managed because, active management has been huge. It's been growing at an explosive rate in terms of equities and fixed income. So we'll be delving into that, especially with the federal reserve kind of keeping the markets guessing at the moment. I think we're pricing in three rate cuts. It was like one rate cut a couple of weeks ago. So you never know which way the market's going to turn. We have the jobs report that was weaker today. And just in terms of other topics broadly, thematics, we'll be talking about

ESG, kind of ESG, but don't call it ESG. there's still a lot of interest in that sustainable investing idea, believe it or not. Our advisory council was very big on making sure we had a panel diving into that. We'll still be talking about crypto, the usual sort of trends that are standing out, although they may have been, on the back burner lately. AI, power demand, lots of interesting narratives going on driving the whole conversation.

Well, crypto was, excuse me, massive last year with the ETFs being launched. So I remember that being a huge theme. I also remember some giant booths from some of these crypto providers in the exhibit hall. I don't know how they get those things there and what they cost, but they were impressive. Yeah, they're shelling out the big bucks for those booths. Yeah, for sure. Sure. So I know you mentioned a few other than your own panel. What kind of panels or topics or keynote speakers are you particularly kind of excited about this year?

Yeah, well, I think one must see panel is led by my dear friend and mentor, Bob Bizani. He's going to be interviewing Rob Arnott of Research Affiliates, and they'll be talking about why you shouldn't reject value investing and, what's not to love there. Rob, of course, has been a pioneer of smart beta. He just launched his new kind of bottom feeders ETF, the research deletion ETF last year. So lots of characters there. We'll have State Street Global Advisors and Bridgewater, executives from both heavyweights and the asset management industry. They'll be on stage with my colleague Todd Rosenbluth to delve into their brand new all weather ETF that just launched yesterday. it's the first ETF that really offers that hedge fund strategy to the average retail

Investor. So really interesting stuff. And, speaking of new launches, lots of buzz again around the new private credit ETFs. Quite a few eyebrows raised there. So we'll hit on this when we talk fixed income with bond blocks and FM investments. Those are two big innovators in the bond ETF space. And, fixed income, again, top of mind for many after a record year for fixed income ETF flows. Then we also got my colleague Roxana Islam. She's going to be talking about under the radar thematic tech trends with an active portfolio manager at T-Row. So it'll be interesting to see what he's watching, given thematics have kind of fallen to the wayside over the past year or so. So we'll see if those pick up this year as more investors look to try to chase alpha.

She's also got an interesting international equity panel with 3Edge and research affiliates, which is a very timely topic in today's economic environment. Again, AI surging power demand, the crypto panel led by Eric Valchunas of Bloomberg, always great on those. And that ESG session again. In terms of, I guess, other speakers, David Kelly, again, great, great speaker, chief global strategist, something of a rock star now among our advisor audience. So we're going to go into deep with one of the largest active managers in the space, him and John Mayer of JP Morgan. Oh, and here's a fun one. We have one called Money Lines and Markets, where Mike Durso from Shorehaven is going to talk to Mike Palm of Circus Sports.

And they're kind of drawing the parallels between investing and sports betting, because there's a surprising amount of quantitative analysis and strategy behind sports betting that can be applied to investing. So I think that's a good example of how we're embodying the spirit of Vegas while we're down there. Mike Palm from Circus is always a real character. And yeah, we'll also have a few practice management advisor wellness sessions with Brian Portnoy. He always does well from Shaping Wealth. he's a leading expert in the psychology of money. We'll be hearing from award-winning speech coaches like Jennifer Morgan from Connective Communication. We'll also have a retirement expert, Ann Lester. Krista Kuberi from Wealth Consulting. The list goes on. And really for holistic business management and wellness practices.

And then Kyla Scanlon always does really well with our younger audiences. she's a young, fresh face, founded bread, huge following on social media. So she's going to be talking about the convergence of social media and AI and the impact that all that's had on the markets. And, just a lot of these sessions, we'll be offering those CE credits. We know everyone has to get them. We want to make it easy for them. As you mentioned, very easy for advisors to sign up. Many of our webcasts, if you attend them lately, you'll be getting free registration passes to the conference. So definitely take advantage of that.

Well, there's definitely a lot there. I'll definitely be going to the sports betting and investing panel. That sounds fun. You mentioned Rob Arnault. He was just on the show. I believe he was either the last episode or the episode before. I could have talked to him for three hours. The guy is a wealth of knowledge. That would be one I would definitely want to go see. So, totally action-packed, a couple of days and not short on information. But you are on a panel this year. You didn't mention your panel. I know there's still some things out there as to, what that is going to be about. But if it's okay for me to ask you a personal question, I just sat on a panel.
Before you do, do you get excited? Do you get a little nervous? Like, how do you prepare? Or do you just go and just wing?

Well, I think, yeah, it's kind of how I prepare for webcasts. I do a few vocal warm-ups, which nobody has to be privy to. But I will usually, chug a lot of hot water. I'll drink some honey tea. And then I'll do my vocal warm-ups, which involve a little bit of singing, a little bit of, just kind of tongue twisters, all the stuff you used to do in drama school. And then I'll just kind of go over my notes and go over the key points that I want to make sure come out in the discussion and be ready to kind of ad-lib from there with follow-up questions. Make sure I'm familiar with my panelists. Make sure they're comfortable with me. Have a little bit of a dynamic going with them.

Maybe learn a thing or two about them, about their hobbies like you did with me, just to kind of see if I can, bring that in and kind of liven up the conversation a bit. It's always a great time connecting with these people, though. I love liaising with these communities. It's one of my favorite parts.

Yeah, and you just led me perfectly into my next question, which is a major draw of this conference is always networking. But the ETF community seems to be so much more open to meaningful connections and community than really any other part of this industry. And I've been in most other parts in some way, shape or form. So, how do you guys think about, as you're setting up this conference, how to facilitate those meaningful connections among attendees, speakers and sponsors?

Yeah, great question. Well, one of the new ways that we are doing that to bridge that gap, we actually have these web-based tools now. We have an app, which we've always had, but this app in particular is going to be very special. It should roll out next week. It's called Exchange 2025. You can download it now, but it won't be of much use yet. But next week, you'll be able to use that and our website to book one-on-one appointments now to make it really easy to engage with attendees at your own leisure. So all registrants will get an invitation and announcement about this. a lot of our advisory council indicated they really prefer the freedom to set meetings for first thing in the morning or later in the afternoon.

At times, whatever's kind of fluid for them in their schedule. So we have a lot of those options. You can meet with anyone you want in a cafe, in what we call the oasis, out on the lawn. Lots of flexibility there. So it feels a little bit less like speed dating, so to speak, and a little bit more just on your own pace. kind of mingling and networking is key because I think that's the real importance. The importance of that community effervescence and kind of feeding off the energy that you get when you're in person with all these people you never know who you're going to bump into. So definitely stress the importance of mingling, networking, just being out there as much as you can.

Yeah, so it can be quite daunting when you attend this event for the first time because it is such a big event. There are so many sessions. There are so many things going on. There are so many different even places. just looking back at Miami, you could be out. There's places. The cabana is out by the pool. There's things upstairs. There's a giant, it's there's a lot going on, which is great. But if you were coming to this conference kind of as a first time attendee, how would you give them some advice on how to navigate not only the event itself, but also to keep up to speed with all the content that's going to be happening?

Yeah, that's a great question. first of all, we're at a new venue. As you mentioned, we're at a brand new, beautiful hotel, Virgin Hotels right off the strip. It's much more reasonably priced. We'll have a wonderful indoor-outdoor experience ready. So we'll have a campus kind of all spread out on a single level. So it'll be easier to kind of find who you're looking for. We want a freer, more interactive feeling, to this conference versus previous conferences. And I think, first off, just to familiarize yourself with the agenda, take a look at the topics or the speakers that kind of resonate with you and your business. Prioritize those. You can, again, use the appointment schedule in your app. Block off times for the sessions that you want to attend.

Think about really the on-site community, who you want to meet, connect with. That's kind of meeting your goals for the day. Be proactive with inviting them to meet you. And, again, never underestimate the importance of networking. Just walk around. You never know who you're going to bump into at a coffee shop. That could cause a great, could close a great deal, create a great connection. You could be your next client, your next prospect. In terms of the weather, I will say it's important to layer up. Vegas is hot, but it might get a little breezy first thing in the morning or even later in the evening. So, I'd say dress code is kind of breathable, business casual. No shorts and flip flops, but it is Vegas.
So, feel free to add a little flair, sparkle, when in Rome, right?

I guess. Yeah. So in addition to kind of the panels and lectures that we talked about, you guys always do some extracurricular type things, whether that's in the morning or... So anything on the agenda this year that really kind of enhances that community connection that you guys generally always kind of sprinkle in there?

Yeah, no, that's true. for one, Vetify has always held a charity event at Exchange to benefit the Susan G. Komen for the Cure Rest Cancer Foundation. And in the past, they've hosted 5K runs, but this year we're doing Putt for Pink. That's mini golf. So we'll have six mini putting greens spread throughout the campus. Attendees can play, engage, donate to a philanthropic cause throughout the week, which I'm really excited for.
Are you much of a golfer yourself, Brad? I am. If I'm allowed to leave for five hours, that is my hobby of choice. Well, there you go.

So hopefully it hit you seeing, putting your heart out there. Also, we have March Madness. It's going to be in full swing. So to mark the occasion, State Street will also be setting up a basketball hoop area. So it's going to be kind of like Basketball Connect 4, which will be fun. So, come on down, shoot your shot and see how you do.
Well, speaking of being March Madness, hopefully people are out of the sports books and in more of the lectures rather than on the strip placing sports bets, you know?
I know. That's true. Sunday might be a tough one to draw the crowd away from the screens, but we'll do our best. It happens.

So the other thing, too, you kind of sometimes always sprinkle in a little bit of a surprise. Last year was a drone show. Not saying you have to have one this year. Anything you got in and you guys are kind of keeping to the wayside that could be a fun little thing?
I'll be honest. If there is, I'm still in the dark about it. So it will be a surprise even to me. So the answer is probably, but I can't confirm or deny at this time.

That's fine. Well, look, I look forward to seeing everybody at the event this year. I'll be there. I'll be recording podcasts. As I told you before we got on, I think I did like 10 or 11 of them last year. And it's always fun to connect with people that have helped me, service providers. It's good to connect with Todd and everybody that I've known and they've been on the show and who are running around that conference. The energy they have to have for that week is intense. But look, I really, really appreciate you spending some time with me. I think it's going to be a great time. But before I let you go, if you haven't signed up already or if you're looking for the agenda,
Where do people need to go to find out more information? Yeah.

So if you haven't yet, don't forget to sign up. We already have more than 1600 registrants and 700 plus advisors and counting. So you can go to our website, exchangeetf.com. We've also been hosting a number of webcasts throughout the month. You can find those on etftrends.com. If you stop by any of those, you'll be able to register for free using a special code. And, we just really want you to have fun networking and enjoying the content with a little bit of levity along the way. So we hope to see you there.
Well, Kirsten, again, thank you so much for your time. And I hope that I run into you while we're there.
Yeah, let's do it. I'll see you on the putting green.
Yeah.
